transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I know the flights are short and safe, but I have this intense, over-the-top fear of getting on a plane that’s now holding me back at work. I finally decided to seek some help because it's really starting to affect my career.
Can you tell me if this fear of flying is the only situation that triggers this intense anxiety, or do you experience similar feelings in other situations or with other modes of transportation?

Yes, this intense fear is strictly limited to flying. I am completely fine with other types of travel, and I'll gladly drive six or seven hours for road trips or beer tastings without any anxiety at all. It is really just airplanes that trigger this panic for me.
Have you been avoiding flying as a result of this fear, and if so, for how long have you been avoiding it?

Yes, I avoid it completely; I'll drive six or seven hours instead of taking a 45-minute flight, and once I even froze at the gate and pretended to be sick so I could leave. While I've always had some mild uneasiness about flying, it has been a constant, severe obstacle for the last two years since my company started requiring these trips.
When you're in a situation where you have to fly, or even just thinking about flying, do you experience any physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling?

Yes, absolutely. Even just seeing a picture of a plane makes my chest tighten, my heart pound, and my palms sweat. The one time I actually made it to the gate, I completely froze up, started shaking, and was breathing so fast I had to leave.
